relations.rationale: Both describe simultaneous actions by Gus but neither logically implies the other.
Gus sipping lemonade has no bearing on Gia checking in teams.
Sipping lemonade doesn't affect whether Ben joked with Gus later.
Gus's drink choice has no connection to Esme's determination.
Gus flipping answer sheets is unrelated to who drove the minibus.
Gus flipping through answer sheets has no relation to laughter from a reminder.
Gus's activity with answer sheets doesn't relate to the number of school houses.
Gus flipping through sheets has no bearing on Esme's age relative to Gia.
Gus flipping through answer sheets could plausibly precede him cheering at final scores, but they are not directly linked causally.
Driving the minibus doesn't imply anything about Ben's height or personality.
Driving the minibus doesn't relate to joking about the picture round later.
If Ben drove the minibus, it directly contradicts the claim that he did not drive it.
Ben driving the minibus has no bearing on Esme's determination.
Bringing pencils and scorecards suggests Kai was prepared and supports the idea he was eager to help set up.
Kai bringing supplies has no bearing on Esme's determination.
Kai's eagerness to help has no connection to Esme's age relative to Gia.
Esme and Kai being in different houses has no bearing on the quizmaster testing a microphone.
Esme and Kai being in different houses is consistent with and doesn't preclude Kai and Gus also being in different houses, but doesn't directly support it either.
Esme and Kai being in different houses doesn't determine whether Esme and Gus are in different houses.
Esme and Kai being in different houses supports the idea that there are multiple houses, consistent with three houses existing.
